plate_findings.evidence: caption: 'bilateral developmental coxa vara'; radiographs show abnormal proximal femoral morphology

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (a, b, c). a: Composite panel of pediatric pelvic/proximal femoral radiographs in a 2-year-old female with bilateral developmental coxa vara; caption identifies the target disease and postoperative radiological results. [raw subtype: bilateral] b: Composite panel of pediatric pelvic/proximal femoral radiographs in a 4-year-old male with bilateral developmental coxa vara; caption identifies the target disease and postoperative radiological results. [raw subtype: bilateral] c: Composite panel of pediatric pelvic/proximal femoral radiographs in a 6-year-old male with unilateral atypical developmental coxa vara; caption explicitly identifies the disease and notes premature proximal femoral epiphyseal closure. [raw subtype: unilateral atypical]

panels.figure_caption: Radiological results for three different cases in the study. a Good radiological results with satisfactory restoration of HEA and FNSA in a 2-year-old female with bilateral developmental coxa vara after removal of the transfixing wires. b Good radiological results with satisfactory restoration of HEA and FNSA in a 4-year-old male with bilateral developmental coxa vara after removal of the transfixing wires. c Good radiological results (apart from premature closure of the proximal femoral epiphysis) with satisfactory restoration of HEA and FNSA in a 6-year-old male with unilateral atypical developmental coxa vara after removal of the transfixing wires
